newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW-China municipal govts seek foothold in HK.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-China municipal govts seek foothold in HK.

text.p: Hong Kong's initial public offering (IPO) market is giving Chinese municipal governments an opportunity to get a foothold in the territory and raise funds by listing Hong Kong-based window companies, analysts say.
Window companies represent Chinese enterprises or government authorities overseas.

"Listing in an international market will help them build up a reputation and pave the way for possible future business expansion in overseas markets," said Kinson Au, senior analyst at PW Asia Brokerage.
Raising funds in China can be more cumbersome than in Hong Kong and with strong demand for red chips, municipal governments were keen to tap the Hong Kong stock market, analysts said.
Red chips are stocks of Hong Kong-based and listed firms with strong Chinese backing.

"I think the main factor is that it provides them with a relatively cheaper and easier way to obtain funding compared with the mainland," said Song Yan-xia, head of research of Bank of China Securities Ltd.
"They can obtain funding at a lower cost and re-invest in their business in China," she said.
Analysts said the listings helped parent companies establish an international profile and gain management experience in Hong Kong.
The new skills and expertise could then contribute to reforming the parent's business in China, said Song.
Hong Kong reverts to China rule in July after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

"Basically there are many window companies eagerly wanting to list on the Hong Kong stock exchange because I think everbody wants to duplicate the Shanghai Industrial story," said Lan Xue, investment analyst at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, the Hong Kong investment arm of the Shanghai municipal government, has been praised as a model red chip.

Shanghai Industrial -- involved in pharmaceuticals, personal care products, tobacco and packaging materials -- issued shares at HK$7.28 each in May 1996 which have hit the HK$28 level on expectations its parent will inject assets into the company.
Apart from the economic environment and industry sector, analysts said a window company's success depends on what the parent is likely to inject into the company.
"I think what we need to have and what we will base our opinion on is what the government or the respective authority intends to do and what is in the pipeline," Xue said.
GZI Transport Ltd, an infrastructural spinoff of Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd, received an enthusiastic welcome from investors last Thursday when it made its market debut.
The stock finished its first day of trading at HK$4.875, up 51 percent from its issue price of HK$3.23.
Through its parent, GZI Transport is indirectly linked to the Guangzhou municipal government.
Shum Yip Investment Ltd, which is backed by the Shenzhen municipal government, is expected to launch a HK$455 million to HK$525 million IPO in February, market sources said.

Tianjin Industrial Holdings Ltd, a retail and industrial investment concern representing the Tianjin municipal government in Hong Kong, is expected to raise HK$1.0 billion through a Hong Kong IPO in the second quarter of 1997, they added.

The sources said Jingtai Co Ltd, backed by the Beijing municipal government, was expected to kick off an IPO in the first quarter of this year, while Chukong Shipping Co Ltd, backed by Zhuhai's municipal government, was expected to list shares in the first half of 1997.
